gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: Tax is calculated on your total annual ___.
gaps.hint: all the money you receive from every source
gaps.explanation: 'Income' is all the money you receive from work, investments, rent and so on during a period.

gaps.sentence: I'm exhausted — I need to ___ down and rest.
gaps.hint: to recline — no object; forms: lie, lay, lain
gaps.explanation: 'Lie' (lie, lay, lain) means to recline and takes no object; 'lay' (lay, laid, laid) means to put something down and takes an object.

gaps.sentence: She wore ___ heels to the party.
gaps.explanation: 'High heels' is the fixed collocation; 'tall' is used for people, buildings and trees.

gaps.sentence: This tooth is ___ and will probably fall out soon.
gaps.explanation: 'Loose' is an adjective meaning not firmly fixed; 'lose' is the verb meaning to no longer have.

gaps.sentence: May I ___ your stapler for a second? Mine has jammed.
gaps.explanation: 'Borrow' = take for a while; 'lend' = give for a while.

gaps.sentence: It's ___ to rain later, so take a coat.
gaps.explanation: 'It's likely to rain' — probable; 'alike' means similar.

gaps.sentence: I couldn't ___ what he was saying because of the noise.
gaps.explanation: 'Hear' means to receive sound; 'listen' means to pay attention deliberately and needs 'to'.
